x: Although my subjects are a little older than this, and you may need to watch for rather more than one season, I would commend to my favoured clients the following promising specimens:-John Dear. Peter Hilliar,Dick Calderwood, Ron Sinclair, Doug Brew, Bob James and Joe Riley.

Chris Steer's effort was particularly good - he improves every time out. D.Brew and R.James indicated we shall be seeing quite a lot more of them - the latter winning the handicap jointly with Adrian Major.

Of the others Doug Brew ran very well in his first attempt at the distance to finish in 67th place. Mike Bullivant broke Jack Brown's course record by over a minute but it should be remembered that conditions were ideal.
Our potential third scorer was Doug Brew, running in his first ever '20' and with laps of 37:38 and 38:28 he was sufficiently well up for us to be leading a close fight for second team place.

John Bicourt, running for the first time over the distance, put in a very good run to lead our team home after having been 'caught in the act' of dropping out by Chris Steer and Doug Brew who were following behind.
Doug Brew made a welcome appearance again after another of his long absences and Denis Jones completed the afternoon by taking the veteran's prize.

These few are also capable of going into the Poly marathon with a real chance of honours, and the much improved John Hall, the unpredictable Doug Brew and our faithful band of stalwart will be there, we hope, to provide the necessary support.
We suffered two casualties - Doug Brew at 10 miles with severe blisters, and Gordon Biscoe running himself to a standstill between 18- 19miles.
On his left is the link man Major the ex-minor who is making a name for himself in the big time. Then there is Scarlet O'Hara and Doug Brew - Doug Brew - I ask you!

Thanks were due to Bill Lucas who was one who bothered to make the journey to cheer the lads on and help deliver some to their various stages; and to Doug Brew who willingly undertook the glamour-less, but important role,of travelling first reserve.

Forty-two Belgravians toed the line and ten finished in the first 34 of the 140 finishers to clinch a win that certainly shook our opponents. Lionel Mann and Bob Smith were in great form to lead our team home with Doug Brew also showing up well to close in our scorers.

Returning to the Belgrave fold after a couple of years absence was Doug Brew and also prominent throughout were Leo Coy and Doug Jardine. Colin Pearson upset Pat O'Connor against the odds and Brian Gorman ('Don't put me in the relay team') had a remarkable run; but for most, onlookers and runners al…

…had an effortless win by over two minutes to take his score up to four consecutive wins around this course. Leo Coy and Doug. Brew both made welcome appearances and must have been surprised by their forward placings.…

John Thresher, who still holds the Club mile record, writes from San Francisco following a reunion with Doug Brew and Chris Steer. We learn that he recently ran his first mile race for 10 years and recorded 4.35!
Also nice to see Doug Brew reappearing from wherever it is he gets to! with a third place in the handicap. Can it be true that this could be yet another comeback?!
